extracted.intended_audience: systematic review authors, Cochrane review authors, and information specialists (librarians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on methods, tools, and safeguards for identifying and screening records when conducting systematic reviews (including living reviews), aimed at improving retrieval efficiency while protecting against missed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic elimination / stopping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The automatic elimination of records using machine‑learning/active learning approaches has not been recommended for use in Cochrane reviews (as of mid‑2023) because more work is needed to develop and validate safe ‘stopping rules’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not automatically discard records without manual assessment until validated stopping rules exist. Further development and validation of statistical stopping criteria are required before automatic elimination is considered safe for Cochrane reviews (see Callaghan & Muller‑Hansen 2020; Li & Kanoulas 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active learning prioritization for screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Active learning processes that prioritize records for screening in order of predicted relevance can enable authors to identify studies most likely to be included much earlier in the screening process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active‑learning/prioritization tools to order screening workloads so high‑relevance records are seen earlier, thereby potentially reducing time to identifying included studies. However, prioritization should not be conflated with automatic elimination; manual assessment remains necessary until safe stopping rules are validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating remaining relevant records (residual estimation)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to estimate how many relevant records remain to be found based on the sample already screened, using recent statistical/machine‑learning methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sampling‑based estimation techniques (see Sneyd & Stevenson 2019; Callaghan & Muller‑Hansen 2020; Li & Kanoulas 2020) to inform decisions about ongoing screening effort and stopping, but treat estimates cautiously and do not use them yet as grounds for automatic exclusion in Cochrane reviews without validated stopping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation for living systematic reviews / evidence surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Automation tools (including machine learning and surveillance pipelines) have increasing support for keeping living systematic reviews up to date, and may be a particularly suitable use case for automation because of available data for machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For living reviews, consider automation for ongoing evidence surveillance to detect new relevant studies; the COVID‑19 pandemic accelerated tool development and case studies report accuracy and manual‑effort savings (e.g., Shemilt et al 2021; Marshall et al 2023). Continue to monitor tool performance and validate before replacing manual processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLP tools to highlight PICO elements and trial characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools using natural language processing can automatically highlight sentences and key phrases (for example PICO elements, trial characteristics, details of randomization) to support reviewers during screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NLP‑based highlighting to assist human screeners by surfacing likely PICO elements and trial features (see Tsafnat et al 2014). These tools are aids to manual screening and can improve efficiency, but reliance should be tempered by evaluation of accuracy and by retaining human judgement for inclusion decisions.
